verdict.rationale: AWS IAM's own documentation shows JSON policies attachable to identities or resources. It lists nine policy types, including identity-based, resource-based, and permissions boundaries, and it controls which AWS resources users can access, which covers resource-scoped least privilege. The evidence does not show condition keys or the documented policy-evaluation logic the story asks for. Missing for 10: evidence of condition elements in policies, documented policy evaluation logic, explicit resource-ARN-level scoping detail, and independent/hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, least privilege is expressible — fine-grained IAM policies with conditions, resource-level scoping, and documented policy evaluation

citations.quote: With IAM, you can manage permissions that control which AWS resources users can access.
Most policies are stored in AWS as JSON documents. AWS supports nine types of policies: identity-based policies, resource-based policies, VPC endpoint policies, permissions boundaries
Manage access in AWS by creating policies and attaching them to IAM identities (users, groups of users, or roles) or AWS resources.
